text:
sana: FYI eu-central1 GPU attach failures spiking, some pods stuck Pending. anyone else?

devops-bot: ALERT: pool=eu-central1-local-nvme read_p99=420ms over 5m; attach_error=ProvisionTimeout; affected_shards=12

peter: digging in 5gnode-312: noticed a simultaneous ephemeral-cleaner run + key-ops re-encrypt kickoff. lots of small random reads on /scratch.

olga: that combination will kill small IOPS. SMART shows temperature climb on several drives. could be thermal throttling.

sana: can we quickly stop ephemeral-cleaner runs and throttle re-encrypt workers? what's the fastest safe action?

noah: stop the cleaner cron (systemctl stop ephemeral-cleaner) and ionice the re-encrypts. I recommend cgroup v2 per-node caps so we don't kill work but limit impact.

peter: commands I ran on a node: `sudo systemctl stop ephemeral-cleaner.service` then created cgroup `/sys/fs/cgroup/rekey` and wrote `io.max="8:0 rbps=40M r_iops=300 wbps=80M w_iops=500"`. moved pids into group.

olga: after caps p99 dropped to ~28ms on sampled nodes and attaches started succeeding. routing fallback enabled to prefer eu-west1 for new GPU attaches for 20m.

sana: devops-bot: record action items and create post-incident ticket.

devops-bot: ACTION: ephemeral-cleaner paused; key-ops re-encrypts rate-limited; routing adjusted prefer-region=eu-west1 for 20m.

noah: follow-ups: 1) add preflight in key-ops to check cluster IO headroom and active cleaner windows 2) schedule re-encrypts staggered by node to avoid concurrent reads 3) add nvme-temp early warning alert to give headroom.

sana: filing INFRA-8321: "avoid concurrent cleaner + re-encrypt causing nvme iops collapse -> gpu attach failures" with playbook (pause, cgroup caps, route flip) and cost estimate for routing failover. assigning to storage + key-ops.

peter: cost note: regional flip adds ~10% short-term egress/latency; prefer this over SLA miss.

sana: monitoring eu-central1 for 30m. will re-enable cleaner in staged batches after we roll out Io caps. :white_check_mark:
